response: A Pyrrhic victory is a term used to describe a victory that comes at a tremendous cost to the victor, making the victory essentially hollow or meaningless. The term originates from the story of King Pyrrhus of Epirus, who defeated the Romans in the Battle of Asculum in 279 BC but suffered such heavy losses that he is said to have remarked, "One more such victory and we are undone." This phrase encapsulates the idea that while the battle was won, the losses were so severe that the victory was not truly beneficial.
